title: Error, offline and failure state design
when: The user needs designed screens and inline states for when loading, saving or connecting fails, instead of a blank or broken area.
inputs: the operations that can fail per view
what the user can do about each
prompt:
Goal: Each failure state says what failed, keeps the user work, and offers a way forward, sized to how much of the screen failed.
Steps:
1. Map failures by scope: one field (inline), one widget (card level), the whole view (page level), the connection (offline banner).
2. Inline and card level: keep the surrounding layout, swap only the failed part for a short message and a Retry button.
3. Page level: a heading in plain words (We could not load your orders), one line on what to do, Retry plus a safe exit link such as Back to home.
4. Offline: a slim banner listening to the online and offline events, with saved work queued and a note that it will sync.
5. Keep everything the user typed; never clear a form because a save failed.
6. Use role="alert" for new errors, calm wording with no blame, and put any code in a small secondary line.
Quality bar:
- Failure size matches what actually failed.
- Each state has one clear next action.
- Error text and icon pass contrast.
Pitfalls:
- Oops! with no next step.
- Full page errors for one failed widget.
- Error states that wipe the form.
Verify:
- [ ] Failures mapped per view and scope.
- [ ] Each has message and action.
- [ ] Alert role present.
- [ ] Retry keeps input.
Output: Markup and styles for each failure state in the page files and style.css.

examples.input: what should the dashboard show when the sales data fails to load
examples.output: sales card shows "Could not load sales" with Retry, rest of dashboard stays, offline banner when the connection drops
